name: PA-13
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+23 partisan lean anchors the race firmly Republican
Incumbent John Joyce holds a massive financial edge: $3.8 million on hand versus roughly $16,000 for Beth Farnham
Prediction markets price Joyce at about 96% to win
No public polling or expert ratings exist, but no evidence points to a competitive race
model.rationale: This south-central Pennsylvania seat is deeply Republican at R+23, Joyce is a well-funded incumbent seeking renomination-and-reelection with $3.8 million banked, and Farnham has raised only about $55,000 with no outside support. Markets and fundamentals agree the Democratic path is negligible, so the forecast sits at a roughly 20-point Republican margin.
model.watch: Any late surge of outside spending against Joyce or a polling surprise showing single digits would be the only signal worth monitoring, though neither appears likely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Pennsylvania's 13th District is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the state, with a partisan lean of R+23. John Joyce, the incumbent, is running for another term and enters the general election with a commanding financial position: more than $3.7 million in cash on hand after raising $2.4 million this cycle.

Democrat Beth Farnham faces steep odds. She has raised about $55,000, holds roughly $16,000 in cash, and has drawn no outside spending on her behalf. No public polls or expert ratings track this race, but prediction markets give Joyce about a 96% chance of winning. The fundamentals, the money gap, and the district's lean all point to a comfortable Republican hold.
